exposure: delivery mode (normal vaginal delivery, forceps delivery, cesarean)
cohort: The study included 578 women who underwent 4-dimensional transperineal ultrasound.
finding: Vaginal delivery, particularly forceps delivery, was significantly correlated with a higher probability of pelvic organ prolapse compared to cesarean delivery and nulliparity.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was significantly correlated with a higher probability of pelvic organ prolapse compared to cesarean delivery, with forceps delivery showing the highest probability.
